details: Bitcoin saw a rebound after President Trump reportedly ruled out a strike on Iran, which helped ease geopolitical tensions. This de-escalation led to a decline in oil prices, US Treasury yields, and the US dollar, improving overall risk sentiment in the market.
title: Bitcoin Rebounds as Geopolitical Tensions Over Iran Eased

details: Cryptocurrency markets experienced over $1 billion in forced liquidations within 24 hours, primarily affecting leveraged long positions. This significant market move was triggered by hawkish Federal Reserve minutes, ongoing geopolitical tensions (including those related to Iran), and warnings about AI threats to crypto security. Bitcoin's brief dip below its trading range exacerbated the liquidations.
title: Over $1B in Crypto Longs Liquidated as Bitcoin Tumbles

details: Bitcoin remains range-bound as macroeconomic headwinds and geopolitical uncertainties limit upside potential. Elevated oil prices continue to support US Treasury yields and the dollar, creating a challenging environment for risk assets like cryptocurrencies. Traders are now keenly awaiting next week's US Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, as softer inflation data could support further crypto gains, while hotter CPI figures combined with negative geopolitical outcomes could put downward pressure on Bitcoin.
title: Macro Headwinds & CPI Report Weigh on Crypto Market
